posts.title: Podcast Episode 3 — He Kept a Page
posts.about:
Two-fourteen. Third floor. The bed stayed empty.

A young officer. Ice on the kitchen glass. Leather shoes in a hallway that should have been ordinary. Then a name too big for a mailbox.
posts.body:
This is a sit. Not a caption. Not a reel.

I walk you through the house, the people you can already meet in Book One, and a night at Malakai Hudson’s walk-up. He was not in the bed. He counted four in, hold, four out, the way his grandmother taught him. A pen hit the desk. One of them went still.

This ain’t a rookie. This is Castellano. Hudson.

Why him. What did he know. What did he see. Three chairs still say Guess Who. I will not name them here. Spin the wheel. Guess. The answers live in the pages.

posts.title: The House Got a Facelift
posts.about:
The homepage is new. The storm is the same.

Walk the house. Then meet the people you’re walking with in Book One — not as a list of strangers. As faces in the weather.
posts.body:
Silver Spine Studio just got a facelift.

Same door. Cleaner walk-through. The Beautiful Beast still sitting in the storm on the homepage — Join Giveaway, Buy Sneak Peek, the dates that matter — where a reader can actually find them.

Hit play on the video. That’s the new house, then the faces.

THE FACES
Elliot Windsor — neuro-surgeon. The rain finds him first.
Det. Gabriel Saxe — the one walking the files when the official story is already typed.
Beatrice Windsor — Aunt Bee. Family. Don’t mistake that for soft.
Judge Halbrook — a name Lancaster kept in a drawer. Unused. The bench after Gatson.

You don’t get their whole truth here. You get to know who you’re walking beside — before the storm decides what it keeps.

posts.title: They Didn’t Knock...But He Did.
posts.body:
Night in the hospital doesn’t sleep the way other nights do.

Elliot Windsor is bandaged, bruised, and supposed to be recovering from the wreck they already wrote off as an accident. Then the doorframe fills with dark suits — one clipboard that never gets a mark on it, one hand locking onto the bedrail like the room already belongs to them.

They didn’t knock.

This is the machine testing how awake a man can be when the official story is already typed, sealed, and waiting for him to stay quiet.

THE BEAUTIFUL BEAST — Book One of the Seven-Fold Chronicle — follows the debt that starts on Colorado’s Million-Dollar Highway and walks into the places that should have been safe.
